purpose: regression check that ADR-0037 did not break the one project that works; NOT a new measurement
headline: no regression — module 1 reproduced 3/8 attempt-for-attempt; module 2 came back 4/8 because ADR-0040 changed its prompt; 7/16 against the control's 6/16

machine.note: quieter than every earlier trial on this stack, which ran at 6-9 GB free

target_modifications: none — package.json gained only 3 Stryker devDependencies; yarn.lock their resolutions (v1 preserved, md5 3597d70b1b11fdd61e4d3ecae0e65968 restored); src/ and test/ empty in git status throughout
environment_deviations: node v22.23.2 via nvm rather than the machine default 20.20.0, which fails this project's engines
yarn 1.22.22 via npx rather than the machine's corepack-shimmed Berry

comparability_correction.finding: prediction 1 was not answerable as asked for module 2
comparability_correction.why: ADR-0040 added the namedClass branch to exportStyleFor, which renders the imports_hint. Module 1 (export default class) hits the pre-existing default branch and its prompt bytes are unchanged. Module 2 (export class) hits the new branch and its prompt bytes changed, so temperature-0 determinism licenses no expectation that its result reproduces.
comparability_correction.observed_how: both hints read out of --dry-run rendered prompts before either run started

1_same_result.verdict: CONFIRMED for module 1, NOT TESTABLE for module 2
1_same_result.module_1: identical: 3/8, 13 attempts, same funnel, same three survivors at the same scores, same 560/700 token medians, same five TS2339 lines
1_same_result.module_2: DIFFERENT: 4/8 rather than 3/8. Direction better. Task hasCellContent:happy_path, which the control quoted in full as a failed candidate. Attributable to the ADR-0040 prompt change, not to ADR-0037.

2_derived_tsconfig_never_fires.premise: project-a tsconfig.json has no include, no exclude and no files, so tsc defaults to every file under the config dir and the candidate in test/ is already in the program
2_derived_tsconfig_never_fires.observed: .sidecrew-tsconfig.json ABSENT from a kept sandbox; .sidecrew-jest.config.cjs and sidecrew.stryker.config.mjs PRESENT
2_derived_tsconfig_never_fires.kept_sandbox_verify: re-verified getBookValue:boundary survivor, SURVIVED score 1.00, 14 killed

3_import_hint_agrees_with_rules.note: 100% over 12 attempts rather than 13; not a decline

adr_0039_reprobe.no_mutants_at_all_tally: still wrong 4 times out of 4 times checked; ADR-0039 is the fix for the fourth, not a fifth instance
adr_0039_reprobe.caveat: isValidationError is plannable now and still absent from plans/importFileUtils-real/test_plan.json, so module 2's denominator covers 4 of 7 helpers rather than 5 of 7

compile_failures.TS2341: buildResultFileName — TIMESTAMP_LENGTH is private; same as the control's fourth quoted failure
compile_failures.TS2304: buildReportFileName — Cannot find name 'randomUUID' x7; NEW. The prompt renders the function's body, which calls randomUUID(), and never the module's import of it. Same cause as the control's InsightsColorEnum failure.

pooling_warning: do not turn 7/16 into a single confidence interval. Module 1's functions carry 12-19 mutants and module 2's carry 1-5, so killed >= 1 is a much lower bar on module 2, where 3 of 4 survivors sit on 1- and 5-mutant functions.

listFiles_is_free.note: marginally faster; the machine had 6 GB more free RAM

adr_0037_specific_confirmations.stripFileList_does_not_leak: tsc printed the whole program's file list alongside 5 diagnostics on a 3,000-file project and the verdict text contains only the diagnostics, byte-for-byte the control's quoted failure. This was the most plausible way for ADR-0037 to regress a working project.

cost.control_comparison: every figure within a few per cent of the control and mostly slightly faster, consistent with 6 GB more free RAM

peak_rss_finding.explanation: RSS measures how much of the model macOS is keeping resident, not how big the worker is. Live ps -o rss on the same unchanged worker read 187.2 MB while free memory was 6.3 GB, and 4538.2 MB was its peak when free memory was 15-16 GB.
peak_rss_finding.consequence: earlier trials' 170-243 MB figures measured a machine under pressure, not a small worker. peak_rss_mb in BatchResult cannot be read as 'what this worker needs', which is how two earlier reports quote it.

new_findings: the rendered prompt shows a function's body and never the imports that body depends on — now twice, on two projects and two modules: InsightsColorEnum and randomUUID. notes is where a planner would put it and notes is never rendered.
peak_rss_mb measures memory pressure rather than the worker
protocol: when a commit under test changes a rendered prompt, identify which modules it changes before the run and report those as fresh draws rather than reproductions
